# Enemies should be aware of the wrap around

## Problem statement

Enemies are currently "wrap-blind": aimed shots always fire a straight line at
the player's raw position (never crossing a screen edge), and enemy movement is
bounded or clamped to the arena, so no enemy ever flies over a screen edge the
way the player ship, asteroids, bullets and the raider patrol already do. The
playfield seam is therefore one-directional — only the player's shots and the
player can cross it — letting the player camp the edges with impunity. Enemy
behaviour should be wrap-aware by default — firing across the seam to reach the
player and flying over the edges — controlled by a per-enemy parameter so a
small set of classic arcade archetypes (Space Invaders march, Centipede) keeps
its bounded, wall-respecting behaviour.

## Users

- **Players** — enemy shots can now arrive from anywhere, including from
  "off-screen" across the seam, so camping a screen edge is no longer a safe
  position. Most enemies occupy the whole wrap-around world rather than a
  bounded box, while the classic set pieces (Space Invaders, Centipede) stay
  recognisible.
- **AI agents / human developers** — one unambiguous data-driven per-archetype
  parameter (`wrapAware`, default `true`) that the game and every gym read
  through the same shared seams, so game↔gym parity is preserved by
  construction and tuning an archetype is a one-field change.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want enemies to fire at me across the screen edge, so that
  hiding against an edge is no longer a guaranteed safe position and shots can
  arrive from the seam exactly like my own wrapped bullets.
- As a **player**, I want most enemies to fly over a screen edge and reappear on
  the opposite side, so the whole wrapped playfield — not a bounded box — is
  part of the arena.
- As a **player**, I want the Space Invaders block and the Centipede to keep
  their classic behaviour (reversing at the walls / weaving within the arena),
  so those recognisable set pieces remain intact.
- As a **developer**, I want a single data-driven `wrapAware` parameter per
  archetype (default: aware) that behaves identically in the game and every
  gym, so enabling or disabling seam-awareness is a one-field change with no
  divergent copies.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Parameter** — Each enemy archetype carries a data-driven boolean
   `wrapAware` (or equivalently named) parameter, defaulting to `true`, wired
   through the existing `EnemyConfig` pipeline so it is visible and editable in
   the enemy editor panel. The `march` (Space Invaders) and `centipede` seed
   configs set it to `false`.
2. **Seam-aware aimed fire** — Aimed shots (Scout, march and the raider's
   aimed fire — every archetype routed through the aimed-shot method) fire
   along the shortest wrapped path to the player: when the direct line is
   longer than the wrap-around route, the shot leaves one edge and arrives from
   the opposite edge (enemy bullets already wrap; AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0). An
   enemy with `wrapAware: false` keeps the current direct aim.
3. **Wrap-aware movement** — Wrap-aware enemy motion (dive, chase, orbit,
   drift, roam, hold-and-move, etc.) that would carry the enemy off-screen
   wraps to the opposite edge (matching the player/asteroid four-edge wrap
   model) instead of being clamped. Non-aware archetypes (`march`,
   `centipede`) are unchanged: march reverses and drops at the arena edge;
   centipede weaves within bounds.
4. **Gym ↔ game parity** — The behaviour is implemented once in the shared
   core (`src/scenes/core/`) and exercised by the affected gym scene(s) and
   `PlayScene` in the same change, so the repo-wide duplicate-body / parity
   guards stay green.
5. **Testing, validation & docs** — Unit tests cover: seam-aware aim angle for
   wrap-aware enemies vs. direct aim for non-aware enemies; position wrapping
   on crossing each edge for wrap-aware motion; config default / CSV wiring
   including the `march` / `centipede` exclusions. The affected documentation
   (`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` and any config-format docs) is
   updated to reflect the change. The full project test suite passes with the
   new changes.

## Constraints

- Do not change the bullet wrap model itself — enemy bullets already wrap and
  expire by lifetime (AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0); this item changes launch direction
  and enemy movement only.
- Exclusions are an explicit seed-config list: only `march` and `centipede`
  default to non-aware. During planning, any other archetype whose classic
  design requires wall interaction belongs in the exclusion list, recorded as a
  code comment and a documented divergence per the gym↔game parity convention
  (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1).
- Implement through the shared core (`src/scenes/core/`), never a divergent
  copy, so the game and every gym run the same code.
- Out of scope: boss behaviours, player ship, minerals, drops, and the bullet
  wrap model itself.
- Written in UK English per repo convention.

## Existing state

- Enemy aimed fire: `Scout.tryFireAimedBullet` computes
  `heading = atan2(target.y - y, target.x - x)` on **raw** positions with no
  seam consideration — the same aimed-shot method is reused for march and
  raider via `ENEMY_FIRE_METHODS` (`src/entities/enemyFire.ts`).
- Enemy bullets: wrap all four screen edges and expire by lifetime
  (AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0; shared bullet path in `src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts`).
- Enemy movement: bounded. Ghost/Grunt clamp to `GAME_WIDTH`/`GAME_HEIGHT`;
  march reverses and drops at arena bounds (`src/scenes/core/marchFormation.ts`:
  `computeMarchBounds` / `advanceMarch`); centipede weaves within bounds;
  formation drift pushes rightward.
- Wrap model to match: player ship and `Asteroid.updatePosition` four-edge
  wrap; `Raider` patrol already wraps; `LaneTraffic` wraps horizontally.
- Enemies are data-driven: `EnemyConfig` (`src/core/configTypes.ts`) + seed
  defaults (`src/core/configDefaults.ts`) + CSV (`src/data/enemy-configs.csv`)
  + enemy editor panel + gym editor.

## Desired change

1. Add the boolean parameter to `EnemyConfig` (`wrapAware`), seed default
   `true`; set `march` and `centipede` to `false`.
2. Seam-aware aim: for wrap-aware entities, compute the player delta along the
   shortest wrapped path before `atan2` in the shared aimed-fire seam; used by
   Scout / march / raider aimed fire (and any other archetype sharing the
   aimed-shot method).
3. Shared post-motion edge wrap: in the shared scene entity loop (game +
   gyms), wrap each wrap-aware enemy's position when it crosses an edge; gate
   on the flag so non-aware archetypes are untouched.
4. Verify per-archetype that nothing breaks (divers mid-dive, chasers,
   orbiters, swarm, formation drift) and adjust tests.
5. Update key docs (`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`; config-format
   docs if they enumerate fields).

## Key Files

- `src/core/configTypes.ts` — add `wrapAware?: boolean` to `EnemyConfig`.
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts` — seed defaults: `true` for most archetypes;
  `false` for `march` and `centipede`.
- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` — new `wrapAware` column entries (if the CSV
  persists the field).
- `src/entities/enemyFire.ts` + aimed-fire call sites (`Scout.tryFireAimedBullet`,
  march, `Raider`) — seam-aware aim.
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — expose the flag and any shared seam support.
- `src/scenes/core/` — shared post-motion wrap (CombatCoreScene / CombatScene
  shared entity loop, alongside the `enemyTargeting.ts` seams).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` + affected gym scenes
  (`GymFodderEnemies`, `GymCentipede`, …) — parity exercises.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — document the parameter and the
  exclusions.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: gameplay feel** — seam-aware aimed fire lets shots come from
  unexpected directions; mitigated by limiting the change to aimed shots
  (radial/spread remain direction-symmetric) and excluding the classic
  archetypes.
- **Risk: wrap × state-machine interaction** — a post-motion wrap applied to
  every wrap-aware archetype could interact with steering that seeks the player
  or with dive/common state machines near the seam (oscillation). Mitigation:
  per-archetype verification during planning and dedicated unit tests at the
  seam.
- **Risk: formation-drift scope** — drift formations that push off-screen wrap
  at the entity level; formation *bases* and shaping logic stay as-is.
- **Scope-creep guard** — seam-aware spread/radial patterns (Q2 option b) are
  out of scope; if wanted later they are tracked as a new work item, not added
  here. Any extra archetype exclusion discovered during planning becomes a new
  work item or is documented as a divergence, not silent scope growth.
- **Assumption: config plumbing** — the parameter lives in `EnemyConfig`
  (CSV-backed, editor-editable), consistent with the established data-driven
  enemy tooling; default `true` for all archetypes except the explicit
  exclusions.

## Related work

- **AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0** — "Bullets should have a distance and should wrap
  around the screen" (completed). Bullets already wrap; this item builds
  directly on that model for launch direction.
- **AH-0MV8BSMXC0097KLW** — "Enemies should emerge from the wormhole" (open).
  Touches the same shared enemy spawn/motion seams; potential overlap to watch
  during planning.
- **AH-0MU4KQ6NT006MP52** — "Extract common enemy base class for regular
  enemies" (completed). `BaseEnemy` hosts the shared config/seam support.
- **AH-0MTFP7EIC004F1MN** — "Enemy Design tooling" (completed). The
  data-driven `EnemyConfig` pipeline this parameter extends.
- **AH-0MTAN4X5D009D7U6** — "Write ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md
  best-practice guide" (completed). The doc updated by AC 5.
- **AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1** — gym↔game parity convention (referenced in
  `AGENTS.md`), enforced by `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Movement scope: which enemies should actually 'fly over the edge'? (a)
  All wrap-aware archetypes — shared post-motion wrap in scene loops;
  march/centipede excluded. (b) Firing only. (c) A curated subset."
  — Answer (Map): "(a)". Source: interactive reply, intake round 1.
- Q2: "Firing scope: which fire patterns become seam-aware? (a) Aimed shots
  only. (b) All patterns."
  — Answer (Map): "(a)". Source: interactive reply, intake round 1.

# Audio Design Chapter — retro-arcade survival game GDD

## Problem statement

The GDD currently defines only SFX (§7.3 Audio Direction) and states background music is out of MVP scope with no musical direction defined. The game lacks a documented musical identity (scales, motifs, harmonic language, instrumentation, dynamic mixing, and state-driven music architecture) to guide composition and implementation when music is eventually built.

## Users

- **Audio designers and composers** — need a definitive musical language (scales/modes, motifs, progressions, instrumentation palette) to write consistent, on-brief music.
- **Technical audio programmers** — need the implementation contract (bus architecture, priority tiers, ducking, state machine, middleware guidance) to build or integrate the music system.
- **Game designers / producers** — need per-game-state emotional targets and transition rules to keep audio aligned with gameplay pacing.

User stories:

- As an audio designer, I want documented scales and motifs per game state, so my compositions match the game's emotional arc without guesswork.
- As a technical audio programmer, I want the music state machine and dynamic-mixing rules defined, so I can implement or configure the music engine against a fixed contract.
- As a producer, I want music explicitly scoped as design reference (out of MVP), so the shipped SFX scope (§7.3) is not disturbed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — New chapter file created:** An **AI Hell Music System** chapter is saved as a Markdown GDD addendum at `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md`. Its **musical substance** is taken from the producer's original *Music & Thematic Audio Design* brief (Phrygian Dominant + Lydian scales; Combat Motifs A and B and the ambient "Star Drift" motif; the combat, boss and ambient progressions; the FM 2–4 operator + chiptune implementation notes — reproduced under **Source material (A)** below) and laid out in the **8-section + 2-appendix** professional structure of the approved reference brief (Ross, v1.0, 16 October 2026): **1** Audio Vision Statement; **2** Musical Identity (2.1 Tonal Language, 2.2 Core Motifs, 2.3 Chord Progressions); **3** Instrumentation Palette; **4** Dynamic Mixing Rules; **5** State-Driven Music Transitions (5.1 Transition Design Principles, 5.2 Transition Matrix, 5.3 Stinger System); **6** Implementation Guidelines (6.1 Audio Middleware, 6.2 Music Event Architecture, 6.3 Parameter Mapping Table, 6.4 Technical Specifications, 6.5 Audio Budget Table); **7** Composer and Sound Designer Briefs (7.1 Composer Brief, 7.2 Sound Designer Brief); **8** Audio Accessibility; **Appendix A** Motif Reference Sheet; **Appendix B** Glossary. The reference brief is a **structure exemplar only** — its Tableau card-game substance (D Dorian, harpsichord/cello ensemble, card-table SFX, parlour ambience) must **not** be imported into AI Hell's chapter.
- [ ] **AC2 — GDD §7.3 references the chapter:** The "Background Music" subsection in GDD §7.3 (Audio Direction) is updated to link the new chapter file, while retaining the explicit statement that background music is **out of MVP scope** (design reference only; SFX remains the only in-scope audio).
- [ ] **AC3 — GDD §8 future-scope row updated:** The "Background music" row in §8 (Future Scope) references the new chapter file so the doc stays self-consistent.
- [ ] **AC4 — Doc-only change, no behaviour impact:** No game code, SFX behaviour, or runtime audio pipeline is changed; existing §7.3 SFX scope and the shipped ToneForge pipeline remain authoritative for the MVP.
- [ ] **AC5 — Validation:** A new docs guard `src/audioDesignChapterDocs.test.ts` (following the sibling `*Docs.test.ts` convention, e.g. `src/powerUpWeaponRosterDocs.test.ts`) asserts, and passes, that: (i) `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` exists; (ii) it carries all 8 numbered sections plus Appendix A and Appendix B of the approved reference structure; (iii) GDD §7.3's "Background Music" subsection links the chapter **and** still states music is out of MVP scope; (iv) the GDD §8 "Background music" row links the chapter. All links resolve, and any index/table-of-contents entries are updated.
- [ ] **AC6 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes** (docs-only; confirms no accidental code impact).

## Constraints

- Music remains **"design reference, out of MVP scope"** — no change to the existing scope stance in GDD §7.3 or §8.
- The chapter is a **synthesis**, not a verbatim import (Q4/Q5, this session): the **musical content** is the producer's original retro-arcade brief reproduced faithfully (Source material (A)); the **document structure** follows the approved reference brief (author: Ross; version 1.0; dated 16 October 2026 — Source material (B)). The reference brief's Tableau card-game substance is **not** carried over.
- Follow the repo's docs naming/style conventions where sensible (singular Markdown addendum under `docs/`, referenced by relative link).
- UK English throughout.

## Existing state

- GDD §7.3 "Audio Direction" covers MVP SFX: baked ToneForge WAV pipeline, SFX event catalogue, per-enemy/per-player audio character, beat-synced explosion accents, and a one-paragraph "Background Music" subsection stating music is a nice-to-have, out of MVP.
- GDD §8 "Future Scope" lists "Background music — Synthwave / retro electronic soundtrack" with no further detail.
- No existing work item implements or specifies background music; the work log contains no musical-identity design doc.

## Desired change

- Add the Audio Design Chapter (AI Hell musical content in the approved reference structure) as a standalone GDD addendum document.
- Point GDD §7.3's "Background Music" subsection and §8's future-scope row at the new document.
- Keep all gameplay/SFX/runtime behaviour untouched.

**Key Files:**
- `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` (new) — the Audio Design Chapter addendum (confirm filename at implementation)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.3 "Background Music" subsection updated with a link + scope note; §8 "Background music" row updated with a link
- `src/audioDesignChapterDocs.test.ts` (new) — docs guard following the sibling `*Docs.test.ts` convention
- `./README.md` (if it indexes docs) — optional link to the new chapter

## Related work

- **Update GDD audio design section and code comments (AH-0MTGS9DZ6001IFJR)** — completed; historical GDD §7.3 SFX additions, unrelated to music direction.
- **Update audio documentation (AH-0MUTYV9QV0000HDT)** — completed; ToneForge baked-asset pipeline docs; source of the current §7.3 scope language.
- **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** — this item.
- See also GDD §7.3 and §8, and `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` for the authoritative SFX cue catalogue.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-stance divergence (medium):** the chapter is "APPROVED FOR PRODUCTION" in tone while the GDD keeps music out of MVP. Mitigated by AC2/AC3 explicitly framing the chapter as design reference; implementation remains a future work item.
- **Middleware references (FMOD/Wwise) are forward-looking:** the game currently uses Phaser/Web Audio with baked assets (§7.3). The chapter's §9 middleware guidance is design intent for future integration, not an instruction to adopt FMOD/Wwise in the MVP. Noted in the chapter context if needed.
- **Content divergence from shipped SFX:** the chapter (§6.4) proposes procedural SFX recipes that differ from the shipped baked-ToneForge SFX catalogue. The chapter is an addendum; §7.3 remains authoritative for MVP SFX (per constraint). Recorded as an assumption.
- **Scope creep:** producer may later want chapter sections mapped into the live audio system — that is future implementation work, tracked separately, not part of this docs-only item.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Where in the GDD should the 'Music & Thematic Audio Design' content live? (a) replace the §7.3 'Background Music' paragraph with the full chapter; (b) keep the paragraph and add a new top-level section; (c) other." — Answer (user): "A — below is a full brief for the music. Use this to create a new file and refer to it from 7.3." Source: interactive reply. The final decision refines (a): rather than inlining, create a **new file** (`docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md`) and **refer to it from GDD §7.3**; adopted as AC1/AC2.
- Q2: "MVP scope statement for music — (a) keep music 'design reference, out of MVP scope'; (b) promote into MVP." — Answer (user): "A." Source: interactive reply. Adopted as the chapter's scope framing (AC2/AC3).
- Q3: "§8 Future Scope 'Background music' row — (a) update to reference the new chapter; (b) leave untouched." — Answer (user): "A." Source: interactive reply. Adopted as AC3.

### Plan-session clarifications (2026-10-23)

- Q4: "What should `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` actually contain? (a) author an AI Hell Music System chapter from the producer's *original retro-arcade* content (Phrygian Dominant + Lydian, Combat Motifs A/B & Star Drift, progressions, FM 2–4 op + chiptune notes) laid out in the approved reference brief's professional structure — the reference brief serving as format exemplar only; (b) import the reference brief verbatim as-is; (c) adapt the reference brief's content to AI Hell's palette; (d) freeform." — Answer (producer): "**1. a**". Source: interactive reply, this plan session. Research: the reference brief describes **Tableau**, a candlelit card game (D Dorian, harpsichord, cello, FMOD, card-table SFX) and is therefore not AI Hell's musical content — AI Hell is a retro-arcade bullet-hell (GDD §1: inspirations Galaxians/classic arcade shoot-'em-ups). The intake session on 2026-10-16 flagged this same conflict and the question was never answered, which left AC1 unverifiable until now. Adopted as the corrected **AC1**.
- Q5: "AC1 enumerates ten sections including *Recommended Scales & Modes* and *Playtesting & Iteration*, but the approved reference brief actually has eight numbered sections plus two appendices and contains no *Playtesting & Iteration* section. (a) correct AC1 to the brief's real structure; (b) keep the ten-section enumeration and build the chapter to it." — Answer (producer): "**2. a**". Source: interactive reply, this plan session. Evidence: reference brief table of contents (Source material (B)). Adopted as the corrected **AC1**.
- Q6: "The full source brief is not embedded in the work item (only section names are), so an implementer cannot reproduce content faithfully and AC1's verbatim requirement is unverifiable. (a) recover the full text from the 2026-10-16 intake session log and embed it in the work item; (b) producer re-supplies the brief." — Answer (producer): "**3. a**". Source: interactive reply, this plan session. Evidence: recovered from session log `~/.pi/agent/sessions/--home-rgardler-projects-AI_Hell--/2026-10-16T11-00-00-344Z_herdr-1792148399-1716826-22311.jsonl`. Adopted as **Source material (A)** below plus the reference-brief record held in this item's comments.
- Q7: Producer additionally instructed: "Also create a follow up work item to implement the design." — Answer (producer): directive recorded verbatim. Source: interactive reply, this plan session. Adopted as follow-up implementation work item **Build the music system from the Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** tracked separately (dependency: the implementation is blocked by this docs item), consistent with the *Scope creep* risk entry and the out-of-MVP scope stance (AC2/AC3).

### Source material (A) — producer's original *Music & Thematic Audio Design* brief (verbatim)

This is the authoritative **musical content** for the new chapter. Reproduced verbatim from the producer's original prompt (2026-10-16). UK-English and retro-arcade framing must be preserved; formatting artefacts in the original (runs such as `♭7Example (E)`) may be repaired into readable Markdown without changing substance.

```markdown
Music & Thematic Audio Design

This section defines the musical identity of the game, focusing on scales, motifs, harmonic language, and usage guidelines across gameplay states. The goal is to merge retro‑arcade space tension (Asteroids) with relentless survival energy (Vampire Survivors), using a coherent musical palette that supports procedural layering and dynamic intensity shifts.

🎼 1. Core Musical Identity

The soundtrack is built around two complementary scales:

Primary Combat Scale — Phrygian Dominant

Used for: wave combat, boss spawns, high‑intensity survival phases.

Scale Formula: 1 ♭2 3 4 5 ♭6 ♭7Example (E): E – F – G♯ – A – B – C – D

Why:

Retro‑arcade tension

Exotic, driving, instantly “space danger”

Works extremely well with FM bass, square leads, and arpeggiators

Provides strong melodic hooks with minimal notes

Secondary Ambient Scale — Lydian

Used for: menus, starfield travel, upgrade screens, low‑intensity exploration.

Scale Formula: 1 2 3 ♯4 5 6 7Example (C): C – D – E – F♯ – G – A – B

Why:

Bright, floating, cosmic

Contrasts the combat scale without breaking aesthetic cohesion

Ideal for pads, shimmering arps, and soft synth textures

🎵 2. Melodic Motifs

Motifs are intentionally short (2–6 notes) to support looping, procedural recombination, and chiptune‑style repetition.

Combat Motif A — “Incoming Wave”

Scale: Phrygian Dominant (E)Contour: Rising tension → abrupt dropNotes: E – F – G♯ – F – E – DUsage:

Triggered at the start of each enemy wave

Can be fragmented into E–F–G♯ for micro‑stingers

Works well as a 3‑note arpeggiated alert

Combat Motif B — “Survival Pulse”

Scale: Phrygian Dominant (E)Rhythmic Cell: Dotted + straightNotes: G♯ – A – G♯ – F – EUsage:

Mid‑combat loop

Easily reharmonized for intensity scaling

Can be doubled with FM bass for crunchy retro drive

Ambient Motif — “Star Drift”

Scale: Lydian (C)Contour: Floating, circularNotes: C – E – F♯ – E – D – CUsage:

Menu screens

Upgrade/shop interface

Slow arpeggiated background texture

🎹 3. Harmonic Progressions

Retro arcade music often avoids complex harmony, but these progressions provide structure while staying loop‑friendly.

Combat Progression (Phrygian Dominant)

E – F – E – D

Minimalist, modal, tense

Works with pulsing bass and rapid arps

Can be expanded to E – F – G♯ – F – E – D – C – D for boss phases

Boss Progression (Phrygian Dominant, extended)

E – C – D – F – E

Chromatic tension

Strong “danger escalation” feel

Supports heavy FM brass or distorted square leads

Ambient Progression (Lydian)

C – D – E – F♯

Bright, drifting, spacey

Works well with pads and slow-moving textures

Can be looped seamlessly or expanded to C – G – D – F♯

🔧 4. Implementation Notes

Motifs should be stored as atomic musical objects (interval sets + rhythm cells) for procedural recombination.

Combat layers should increase harmonic density (more voices, faster arps) rather than changing the motif.

Ambient layers should use long‑release envelopes and minimal rhythmic content.

FM synthesis (2–4 operators) and chiptune waveforms (square, triangle, noise) define the retro palette.

All motifs should be designed to loop cleanly at 1–2 bars for dynamic layering.
```

### Source material (B) — approved reference brief (structure exemplar)

The full 58 KB reference document (Ross, v1.0, 16 October 2026) that defines the **chapter structure** is recorded verbatim in a comment on this work item titled *Source material (B) — approved reference brief (structure exemplar), verbatim*. It describes the card game **Tableau**; treat its **section architecture, table layouts, parameter/stinger/matrix formats and glossary style** as the template, and its **musical and SFX substance as out of scope**.

## Verification approach

Docs-only change, but the repo convention is that cross-cutting docs slices ship with a `*Docs.test.ts` guard
(12 sibling guards exist, e.g. `src/powerUpWeaponRosterDocs.test.ts`, `src/enemyRosterDocs.test.ts`). The guard
for this item asserts file existence, the reference-brief section structure, and both GDD cross-links —
including the "out of MVP scope" sentence, so a future edit cannot silently promote music into the MVP.

Manual checks that complement the guard:
- Open `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` and confirm every Source material (A) element maps into the document
  (two scales, three motifs, three progressions, four implementation notes) — nothing dropped, nothing invented.
- Confirm no Tableau substance leaked in (no D Dorian as the home mode, no harpsichord/cello ensemble, no
  card-table SFX).
- Confirm §7.3's SFX catalogue, autoplay and rate-limiting text is untouched (AC4).

AC6 is satisfied by the standard dev-push gate (full suite); the guard above gives the changed-scope signal.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MT7UW0Y80062NU1** – Bring simple audio effects into MVP scope in GDD (interactions, impacts, enemy actions, advanced telegraphing) (completed)
- **AH-0MUTYV9QV0000HDT** – Update audio documentation (completed)
- **AH-0MTGS9DZ6001IFJR** – Update GDD audio design section and code comments (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: audio, design, gdd, music, update
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: audio, design, music, update
- `README.md` — matched: audio, design, gdd, update

# Make Phase Shift and wormhole-emergence effects unmistakable

## Problem statement

The improved Phase Shift / wormhole-emergence treatment shipped under
AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S (commits 4267a534, 4b407b66, eafc45b6, c84c1a99, 5b5877e4) is
technically complete and audited, but **the producer reports it is still not
noticeable enough — the effect must be unmistakable**. The intent of the original
epic ("instantly obvious that they are not in their usual state") is therefore not
yet satisfied in practice, even though every written acceptance criterion passed.

Producer feedback (2026-10-25, verbatim): *"These effects are not noticeable
enough, needs to be unmistakable."*

## Users

- **Player (primary):** "As a player, the instant my ship phases out — or enemies
  start materialising out of the wormhole — I want to *know* without looking for
  it. Not a tint I have to hunt for: an unmistakable event."
- **Player (defensive read):** "As a player relying on the automatic Phase Shift, I
  want the activation to read like a system event (a hit, a pulse, a distortion),
  not a subtle colour shift, so I can trust it and time my flying."
- **Developer / maintainer:** "As a developer, I want whatever stronger treatment we
  choose to live once in the shared VFX layer, stay toggleable per layer, and keep
  the gyms and the game pixel-identical."

## Current state (what shipped, and why it reads as subtle)

Screen-wide Phase Shift (`src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts`):

| Layer | Current value |
|---|---|
| Dim overlay | dark blue 0x0a1a33, alpha 0.22 |
| Chromatic split | cyan 0x33ffee / red 0xff3355, **alpha 0.20**, base offset **6 px** (+/-1.5 px, 1.6 s) |
| Alpha flicker | 3 Hz, 25 % depth |
| Colour pulse | 0.75 -> 1.0 cross-fade |
| Activation burst | alpha 0.35 at +/-12 px, 200 ms fade |
| Camera shake | **deliberately none** (producer decision: it read like death juice) |

Per-enemy emergence (`src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts` `updateEnemyShimmer`):
ripple burst +0.06 scale / +0.15 alpha over 200 ms, then alpha flicker 0.55-0.85 at
3 Hz, scale pulse 4 %, additive-bloom colour pulse (Phaser 4 `Container`/`Graphics`
have no Tint).

Wormhole ring (`attachWormholeRing`): 0xd9b3ff, r 52 px, 3 px stroke, alpha 0.45,
yoyo scale 0.9-1.15 every 900 ms.

Diagnosis of the shortfall (to be confirmed with the producer): every layer is a
**low-alpha translucent tint at screen-wide scale**, and translucency over a busy
bullet-hell background is perceptually weak. "Unmistakable" most likely needs
*high-contrast, structural* change — distortion, a hard flash, silhouettes, motion —
not just larger alpha values.

## Candidate approaches (producer to choose / amend)

**A — Bigger same-technique (lowest risk, no new rendering technique).**
Split alpha 0.20 -> ~0.45 and offset 6 -> ~14 px; burst alpha 0.35 -> ~0.70 at
+/-28 px over ~320 ms; add a short full-screen brightness flash on activation
(distinct palette from the death flash); add cyan edge/vignette bands during phase
(the defeat-screen vignette technique) so the *frame* changes, not just the objects;
per-enemy alpha flicker range widened (e.g. 0.25-1.0) plus a stroked silhouette
outline per emerging enemy; wormhole ring radius/alpha raised with an open shockwave.

**B — Real screen-space distortion via Phaser camera post-FX (highest impact).**
Use the engine's built-in post-FX pipelines on the main camera while phased: a
short displacement/pixelate wobble on the activation edge, then a sustained subtle
`Bloom`/`Glow` + gentle `Barrel`/`Displacement` wobble, all driven from the same
tunables. This is the genuine "glitch" read and is far more visible than alpha
tints. Caveats: the original epic explicitly scoped shader/render-to-texture work
out; needs a WebGL check + a headless-safe fallback, a measurable perf check, and a
canvas-renderer degradation path. Phaser post-FX state must also be torn down
exactly on the falling edge.

**C — Combination (recommended by the agent, producer decides).**
A for the player + wormhole (cheap, robust) **plus** B's activation-edge distortion
burst only (a ~150-250 ms pixelate/displacement hit), so the *event* is unmistakable
while the *sustained* state stays comfortable.

## Constraints

- **Gym<->game parity** (AGENTS.md): the behaviour lives once in `src/vfx/*` and the
  shared spawn path; `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel` and the combat gyms
  consume the same code. The duplicate-body guard and the gym-parity docs assertion
  must stay green.
- **No camera shake** unless the producer explicitly reverses that decision. (The
  regression test asserting "never shakes" currently encodes it.) If a shake-free
  "punch" is wanted, prefer camera **zoom** punch or post-FX over shake.
- **Seizure safety:** a genuinely unmistakable effect must still avoid rapid strobe.
  If flicker frequency rises, cap it (~<=3-4 Hz for sustained layers) and add an
  explicit accessibility toggle; a reduce-motion option remains a separate item.
- **Per-layer toggles and pure params model** are retained (`PHASE_SHIFT_ENABLE_*`,
  `ENEMY_SHIMMER_ENABLE_*`, `WORMHOLE_RING_ENABLE`, pure `resolve*Params()`).
- **Headless-safe:** no-op without a Phaser render context; unit tests stay
  deterministic.
- **Performance-neutral to near-neutral:** no per-frame allocations; post-FX, if
  chosen, needs a measured cost check on the existing target hardware.
- **Visual distinctness from player-death juice** must be preserved and asserted.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Unmistakable activation read (player) — aggressive edge.** On the frame Phase Shift activates (`isPhased` rising edge) the treatment produces a *structural, high-contrast* hit, not merely a tint: (a) a short (~150–250 ms) **screen-space distortion burst** via Phaser 4 camera filters (pixelate + barrel/displacement wobble), (b) a brief **full-screen flash** in a phase-shift palette (explicitly not the player-death flash palette), and (c) a widened, stronger chromatic-surge overlay pair. Every magnitude is an exported tunable and every layer has its own `PHASE_SHIFT_ENABLE_*` toggle.
- **Unmistakable sustained read (player) — soft sustained.** While `isPhased` stays true the state stays continuously obvious without being aggressive: the vivid pulsing chromatic split (raised alpha/offset with slow oscillation), a cyan edge/vignette band layer, and a gentle sustained camera-filter layer (low-strength glow/bloom or barrel) — flicker capped at <=3-4 Hz for seizure safety, and **no camera shake**.
- **Exact teardown / no residual state.** On the falling edge every overlay, tween and camera filter added by the treatment is removed and the camera filter list is restored to its pre-activation state; a second expiry, a scene `SHUTDOWN`, or a re-activation cycle leaves no residual tint, no leaked filter controller and no duplicated layer.
- **Renderer capability probe + graceful fallback.** Camera filters are WebGL-only: the treatment applies filter layers only when the renderer supports them, and otherwise degrades to the overlay-only layers, never throwing (headless/canvas tests exercise the fallback path).
- **Unmistakable emergence read (enemies) — per-entity only.** Each enemy growing from the wormhole is individually unmistakable as "not solid yet" for its whole `ENEMY_GROWTH_DURATION`: a stronger ripple burst at growth start, a widened alpha flicker, a scale pulse and a per-entity **outline/silhouette** ring so the entity's shape visibly shimmers; driven from the shared spawn path (`updateSpawnAnimation` -> `updateEnemyShimmer`); the entity's own alpha/blend/scale state is fully restored when growth ends; **no screen-wide overlay** on the emergence path.
- **Wormhole read.** The open wormhole is unmistakably the source of the emergence: a larger/brighter pulsing ring plus a one-shot shockwave/light pulse when it opens, drawn once per wormhole, tracked in the existing `wormholeEffects` registry, and fully cleared (tweens stopped, objects destroyed) when the wormhole closes.
- **Distinctness, parity and no regressions.** The treatment stays visually distinct from player-death juice (asserted), **never shakes the camera** (regression test retained), the gym<->game duplicate-body guard and gym-parity docs assertion stay green, and headless construction/update is a safe no-op.
- **Tests and docs.** Unit tests cover the new tunables/toggles, the activation burst layers, the sustained layers, filter application/teardown, the WebGL-unavailable fallback, the per-entity outline lifecycle, the wormhole shockwave lifecycle, the no-shake regression and headless no-op. `docs/Game Design Document.md` section 7.2 and the code comments document the final treatment and every new constant. The full project test suite passes.

## Producer decisions (2026-10-25)

- **Q1 = C** — combination: approach A (bigger same-technique + frame-level flash/vignette/silhouette) everywhere, **plus** approach B's screen-space distortion for the player path.
- **Q2 = iii** — aggressive on the activation edge, soft for the sustained state.
- **Q3 = no shake** — the no-camera-shake decision stands; the "punch" comes from post-FX/flash layers only. The existing regression test stays.
- **Q4 = ship and iterate** — the epic AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S is **not** held: no dependency edge from the epic to this item; it releases through the normal dev->main gate and this item improves the effect afterwards.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Which approach?** (A) bigger same-technique only; (B) real screen-space post-FX distortion for the player path; (C) combination.
  — Answer (producer, 2026-10-25): **C**. Rationale: keep the robust overlay/vignette/silhouette work everywhere and add a genuine distortion read for the player's activation.
- **Q2 — How far may intensity go?** (i) comfortably strong; (ii) aggressive/startling; (iii) aggressive activation edge, soft sustained.
  — Answer (producer, 2026-10-25): **iii**. Rationale: the *event* must be unmistakable; the *state* must stay comfortable for the whole phase duration.
- **Q3 — Revisit the no-shake rule?** (i) keep no-shake, use post-FX/flash instead; (ii) allow a short low-intensity shake on the activation edge only.
  — Answer (producer, 2026-10-25): **no shake**. Rationale: preserves the established distinctness from player-death juice.
- **Q4 — Release hold for the epic AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S?** hold its release until this lands, or ship and iterate.
  — Answer (producer, 2026-10-25): **ship and iterate**. No blocking edge is wired from the epic to this item.

## Technical feasibility note (verified before planning)

Phaser 4.2.1 exposes camera filters (`camera.filters.internal` / `.external`):
`addPixelate`, `addBarrel`, `addGlow`, `addVignette`, `addBlur`, `addParallelFilters`
(bloom), `addDisplacement`, `addColorMatrix`. They are **WebGL only**, so the driver
must probe `scene.game.renderer.type` / `camera.filters` and degrade to the
overlay-only layers otherwise. No post-FX is used anywhere in `src/` today, so this is
a new (but engine-supported) technique.

## Constraints

- **Gym<->game parity** (AGENTS.md): the behaviour lives once in `src/vfx/*` and the
  shared spawn path; `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel` and the combat gyms
  consume the same code. The duplicate-body guard and the gym-parity docs assertion
  must stay green.
- **No camera shake** unless the producer explicitly reverses that decision. (The
  regression test asserting "never shakes" currently encodes it.) If a shake-free
  "punch" is wanted, prefer camera **zoom** punch or post-FX over shake.
- **Seizure safety:** a genuinely unmistakable effect must still avoid rapid strobe.
  If flicker frequency rises, cap it (~<=3-4 Hz for sustained layers) and add an
  explicit accessibility toggle; a reduce-motion option remains a separate item.
- **Per-layer toggles and pure params model** are retained (`PHASE_SHIFT_ENABLE_*`,
  `ENEMY_SHIMMER_ENABLE_*`, `WORMHOLE_RING_ENABLE`, pure `resolve*Params()`).
- **Headless-safe:** no-op without a Phaser render context; unit tests stay
  deterministic.
- **Performance-neutral to near-neutral:** no per-frame allocations; post-FX, if
  chosen, needs a measured cost check on the existing target hardware.
- **Visual distinctness from player-death juice** must be preserved and asserted.

## Acceptance Criteria (draft — finalise after producer answers Q1-Q3)

- **Unmistakable activation read (player).** On the `isPhased` rising edge the
  treatment produces a structural, high-contrast change (not merely a tint): the
  chosen mechanism (A/B/C) fires within the same frame and is perceptible against a
  busy background in a manual play check; magnitudes exported as tunables with
  per-layer toggles.
- **Unmistakable sustained read (player).** While phased, the state remains
  continuously obvious for the whole duration (chosen sustained layer(s) from A
  and/or B), with the no-camera-shake guarantee intact and every layer torn down on
  the falling edge (no residual tint or residual post-FX state).
- **Unmistakable emergence read (enemies).** Each emerging enemy is individually
  obvious as "not solid yet" across its whole `ENEMY_GROWTH_DURATION` window, driven
  from the shared spawn path; the entity's own render state is fully restored when
  growth ends; no screen-wide overlay on the emergence path.
- **Wormhole read.** The open wormhole is clearly the source of the emergence (ring
  and/or column strengthened per the chosen approach), tracked in the existing
  `wormholeEffects` registry and fully cleared on close.
- **No regressions.** Death juice stays visually distinct; the no-shake regression
  holds (unless the producer reverses it, in which case it is updated deliberately);
  gym<->game parity guards pass; headless no-op tests pass.
- **Tests and docs.** Unit tests cover the new tunables/toggles, the new
  layers/mechanism creation + teardown (including post-FX teardown if chosen), and
  the no-shake and headless guarantees. `docs/Game Design Document.md` section 7.2
  and the code comments are updated with the final magnitudes. The full project test
  suite passes.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) — magnitudes, new layers, optional
  camera post-FX driver.
- `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) — per-enemy treatment, wormhole ring.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — shared driver (post-FX needs a camera).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts` — consume the shared helpers only (no new behaviour).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` section 7.2 — final treatment + tunables.

## Related work

- **AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S** (completed, audited, awaiting release) — the epic that
  delivered the current treatment. This item is `discovered-from:AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S`.
  The producer must decide whether the epic's release is held until this lands.
- AH-0MVD2MXAB004K0V4 — player phase-shift juice (vivid split + burst + shimmer).
- AH-0MVD2N333004VDA9 — per-enemy emergence shimmer.
- AH-0MVD2N6AW0073X5M — wormhole glow/pulse ring.
- AH-0MUJRGWGG0073JWS — original Phase Shift juice module (dim + split, no shake).
- AH-0MUTV7632000ZWCB — end-of-run juice; the defeat glitch-flicker + vignette
  technique is the precedent for approach A's frame-level layers.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: seizure sensitivity / discomfort** — "unmistakable" pushes toward higher
  contrast and faster flicker. Mitigation: cap sustained flicker, keep the aggressive
  part on the short activation edge, keep per-layer toggles, and track a
  reduce-motion accessibility option separately.
- **Risk: post-FX complexity and platform variance** (approach B) — WebGL-only,
  needs canvas fallback, exact teardown, and a perf measurement. Mitigation: fall
  back to approach A layers when post-FX is unavailable.
- **Risk: parity drift** — mitigated by implementing once in the shared VFX layer;
  guards enforce it.
- **Assumption:** the producer's "unmistakable" means *perceptually unavoidable*,
  not necessarily *physically larger* — the chosen mechanism is a producer decision
  (Q1-Q3 above).

# Unit tests: player Phase Shift unmistakable layers

Test-first contract for the player path of AH-0MVNTR89P0022JIU (approach C,
aggressive activation edge / soft sustained state). Write these as failing
tests first; the implementation children make them pass.

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the *unmistakable* player treatment pinned by tests
before it is built, so the layers, magnitudes, toggles and teardown cannot
regress and the no-shake guarantee cannot be silently dropped.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Pure params model.** `resolvePhaseShiftJuiceParams()` maps every new tunable
  and `PHASE_SHIFT_ENABLE_*` toggle verbatim (flash, vignette, distortion burst,
  sustained filter, widened split), with no Phaser import in the pure path.
- **Activation edge (aggressive).** A single `update(true, dt)` rising edge
  creates the full activation layer set — dim + split + surge pair + full-screen
  flash + vignette + the camera-filter distortion burst — exactly once, and a
  second `update(true, dt)` in the same phase does not duplicate any layer.
- **Sustained state (soft).** While active, deterministic `dt` ticks drive the
  split oscillation/flicker/colour-pulse and the sustained filter layer without
  allocating new game objects per frame (asserted by object-count stability
  across N ticks).
- **Exact teardown.** On the falling edge every overlay is destroyed, every
  camera filter added by the treatment is removed from the camera filter list,
  the registry is emptied, and a re-activation cycle produces a fresh, single
  layer set (no leak, no duplicate).
- **Renderer fallback.** With the renderer reporting non-WebGL (or a camera with
  no `filters`), the treatment applies the overlay layers only, never throws and
  never touches a filter API; the same suite passes headless.
- **No camera shake.** The retained regression test still asserts the treatment
  never calls `camera.shake` in any phase of the cycle.
- **Test style.** Deterministic (`dt` ticks, no sleeps/randomness), using the
  shared `VfxStubScene` / `bootScene` harness.

## Key Files

- `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.test.ts` — extend.
- `src/vfx/cameraFilters.test.ts` — new (probe/apply/clear contract, shared with the enemy path if reused).

## Notes

Tests must not require a real WebGL context: stub the camera filter list with a
minimal fake exposing `internal`/`external` `add*` factories, `list`, `remove`,
`clear`.

# Unit tests: unmistakable enemy emergence + wormhole ring

Test-first contract for the per-entity and wormhole parts of AH-0MVNTR89P0022JIU
(approach C: no screen-space effects on the emergence path).

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the unmistakable emergence treatment and the wormhole
ring/shockwave pinned by tests before implementation, so the per-entity
lifecycle (create -> shimmer -> release) and the ring lifecycle cannot regress.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Per-enemy outline/silhouette.** `updateEnemyShimmer` creates exactly one
  outline/silhouette layer per emerging entity on its first shimmering frame,
  pulses it during the growth window, and destroys it when growth ends.
- **Widened flicker + burst.** The alpha flicker range and the leading-edge
  ripple burst magnitudes are driven verbatim from exported tunables; the burst
  decays to zero within its documented window.
- **No residual state.** After growth ends the entity's alpha, scale and blend
  mode are restored to their pre-shimmer values, the outline is gone, and the
  per-entity shimmer clock is dropped; an entity that never shimmered is
  untouched.
- **No compounding.** Running the helper twice per frame (or with variable `dt`)
  leaves the growth scale correct (absolute-value write, no drift).
- **Wormhole ring + shockwave.** `spawnWormholeOpen` creates one ring (and one
  open shockwave pulse) per wormhole, registers them in the caller's
  `wormholeEffects` registry, and `spawnWormholeClose` stops their tweens and
  destroys them exactly once (a second close or a `SHUTDOWN` does not
  double-remove).
- **Headless no-op.** All helpers construct/update with a stubbed scene (no
  `add`/`tweens`) without throwing.
- **Test style.** Deterministic scene-tick steps (`scene.tick(dt)`), no sleeps.

## Key Files

- `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.test.ts` — extend.

# Camera filter driver with WebGL capability probe

Shared infrastructure for approach C of AH-0MVNTR89P0022JIU: Phaser 4 camera
filters are **WebGL only**, so every filter-based layer needs one guarded,
teardown-exact entry point.

## Goal

As a developer, I want a single shared module that can apply and clear the
Phase Shift camera-filter layers safely on any renderer, so the game and the
gyms never diverge and a headless/canvas build can never crash or leak.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Capability probe.** `supportsCameraFilters(scene)` returns true only when
  the renderer is WebGL *and* the camera exposes a usable filter list; it never
  throws for a stub, a missing camera, or a renderer without `type`.
- **Activation burst.** `applyPhaseDistortionBurst(...)` adds the pixelate +
  barrel/displacement wobble controllers for the documented duration, driven by
  the exported tunables (no hard-coded numbers).
- **Sustained layer.** `applyPhaseSustainedFilter(...)` adds the gentle
  sustained layer (low-strength glow/bloom or barrel) and returns handles for
  teardown.
- **Exact teardown.** `clearPhaseFilters(...)` removes and destroys only the
  controllers this module added, restoring the camera's pre-existing filter
  list unchanged (verified by a test that pre-adds an unrelated filter and
  asserts it survives).
- **Degradation.** When filters are unsupported every function is a documented
  no-op returning a falsy/"unsupported" result; nothing is allocated.
- **No per-frame allocation.** Steady-state updates mutate existing controller
  properties only.
- **Documented.** Module-level JSDoc explains WebGL-only behaviour, the fallback
  contract and every tunable.

## Key Files

- `src/vfx/cameraFilters.ts` — new.
- `src/vfx/cameraFilters.test.ts` — new (see sibling test item).

# Player Phase Shift unmistakable treatment

Implementation of the player path for AH-0MVNTR89P0022JIU: aggressive on the
activation edge, soft while sustained, never shaking the camera.

## Goal

As a player relying on the automatic Phase Shift, I want the activation to read
as an unmistakable system event — a flash, a distortion hit and a strong
chromatic surge — then settle into a clearly-visible sustained shimmer, so I can
trust the state and time my flying.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Activation edge (aggressive).** The rising edge fires, in the same frame:
  a widened/stronger chromatic-surge overlay pair, a full-screen flash in a
  phase-shift palette (not the death-flash palette), a cyan edge/vignette band
  layer, and the camera distortion burst from `cameraFilters.ts`.

  (raised alpha and offset with the slow oscillation), the edge/vignette bands
  and the gentle sustained camera filter, all pulsing rather than static;
  sustained flicker stays at or below the documented seizure-safety cap.
- **Exact teardown.** Falling edge removes every overlay, tween and camera
  filter; nothing is left on screen or in the camera filter list.
- **Toggles and tunables.** Each new layer has a `PHASE_SHIFT_ENABLE_*` toggle
  and every magnitude is an exported constant; disabling a layer leaves the rest
  working.
- **No shake.** `camera.shake` is never called (regression test retained).
- **Headless safe.** Without a render context the controller still constructs
  and updates as a no-op.
- **Tests.** The sibling test contract item passes.

## Key Files

- `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts` — tunables, `_apply`/`_pulseShimmer`/`_clear`.
- `src/vfx/cameraFilters.ts` — consumed for the filter layers.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — shared driver (unchanged call shape).
